segments.text: Pilots train in simulators. Ops rooms don't.
This is Fly-Through, on a fog morning at a Gulf hub.

Fog closes the hub at five fifty-two, and sixteen flights divert to four airports. Six AI agents, one in each seat of the war room, call out what they see. Every number comes from a tool, and each call-out shows the tools behind it.
Each seat keeps its own thread. Crew Control watches the duty clocks: three crews will time out before the fog lifts.
At six fifty-eight the sim pauses. All six seats debate three plans in two rounds, each arguing from the criterion it owns, and each naming a risk.
Safety is a gate, not a score. Then six airline criteria are weighed.
Only a human can approve. Standby crews board buses through the fog, with live arrival times.
At eight thirty the forecast changes: the fog now lifts at ten forty-five, and three more crews would time out. The room debates again, and the AI flags where its judgement differs from the numbers.
The human approves again. Reserve crews head out to Al Ain, Sharjah and Dubai.
When the hub reopens, aircraft fly home in arrival slots, each with a crew that is legal to fly.
Sixteen aircraft home. Rehearse the bad day before it comes.
